observations: A flat-brimmed rectangular hat sits across the upper portion of the figure, its edges defined by bold black outlines filled with dense crossing lines in lime green, red, gold, and magenta against a solid turquoise background.

Two eye areas occupy the mid-section: the right is built from a tight circular spiral; the left from a dark inward-pointing triangular wedge—both embedded in overlapping short strokes of white, pink, blue, and green.
A wide horizontal band near the lower face is outlined in thick black and gold with white interior gaps suggesting teeth, sitting above a loosely sketched neck area in the lower quarter.
reading: The figure is assembled from stacked rectangular zones—hat, brow, eye band, mouth bar—each packed so densely with crossing lines that the underlying form feels pressurized rather than drawn. The turquoise field holds everything at a cool distance while the interior burns with lime, magenta, and red. One eye spirals outward; the other collapses into an angular wedge. That asymmetry gives the face an unsettled quality the rigid geometry alone would not produce.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between 'nnxyz nifty faces #16' and 'nnxyz nifty faces #18' in both title order and recorded creation order. Where #16 spreads fragmented shards across a yellow field, #17 compresses everything into a single upright column against flat turquoise, making containment the dominant contrast.

connections.reason: Both works use dense multi-color crossing lines to build a face, but #16 fragments outward across a yellow ground while #17 holds its form tightly upright against turquoise—a direct contrast of expansion versus compression.

#18 shares the asymmetric eye treatment—one circular, one crossed—and a rectangular mouth band, but replaces #17's structured hat with an open scribble fringe along the top edge, showing how a single changed element shifts the overall feel.

lookingQuestion: The two eye areas are built from opposite mark types—one a tight spiral, one a dark angular wedge. Where else in the image do you notice curved and straight lines occupying the same zone?
ambiguities: Title order and recorded creation order align for this work, but the metadata notes gaps and variants exist elsewhere in the family, so this alignment cannot be generalized.

The nnotb #116 comparison image was inspected but shows a yellow-ground composition with bold isolated blue stripes and distinct facial symbols; no strong formal connection to #17 was found, so it was omitted.
